# Resource: tfe_admin_smtp_settings

(Only for Terraform Enterprise) Creates, updates, and destroys Admin SMTP settings.

Requires admin token configuration. See example usage for incorporating an admin token in your provider config.

## Example Usage

```python
import constructs as constructs
import cdktf as cdktf
# Provider bindings are generated by running cdktf get.
# See https://cdk.tf/provider-generation for more details.
import ...gen.providers.tfe as tfe
class MyConvertedCode(cdktf.TerraformStack):
    def __init__(self, scope, name):
        super().__init__(scope, name)
        # Terraform Variables are not always the best fit for getting inputs in the context of Terraform CDK.
        #     You can read more about this at https://cdk.tf/variables
        admin_token = cdktf.TerraformVariable(self, "admin_token",
            description="An admin access token"
        )
        hostname = cdktf.TerraformVariable(self, "hostname",
            default="app.terraform.io",
            description="The HCP Terraform or Enterprise hostname."
        )
        tfe.admin_smtp_settings.AdminSmtpSettings(self, "this",
            auth="none",
            host="smtp.example.com",
            port=25,
            sender="noreply@example.com"
        )
        tfe.provider.TfeProvider(self, "tfe",
            hostname=hostname.string_value,
            token=admin_token.string_value
        )
```

```terraform
# With write-only password

variable "admin_token" {
  description = "An admin access token"
}

variable "hostname" {
  description = "The HCP Terraform or Enterprise hostname."
  default     = "app.terraform.io"
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  type      = string
  ephemeral = true
}

provider "tfe" {
  hostname = var.hostname
  token    = var.admin_token
}

resource "tfe_admin_smtp_settings" "this" {
  host                = "smtp.example.com"
  port                = 587
  sender              = "noreply@example.com"
  auth                = "login"
  username            = "smtp_user"
  password_wo         = var.smtp_password
  password_wo_version = 1
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth` (String) The authentication type. Valid values are `none`, `plain`, and `login`. Defaults to `none`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether SMTP is enabled. When enabled, all other attributes must have valid values.
- `host` (String) The hostname of the SMTP server.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password used to authenticate to the SMTP server. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`. Cannot be used with `password_wo`.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The password used to authenticate to the SMTP server, guaranteed not to be written to plan or state artifacts. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`. Either `password` or `password_wo` can be provided, but not both. Must be used with `password_wo_version`.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Version of the write-only password. Used to trigger updates when the write-only password changes. Must be used with `password_wo`. When `password_wo_version` changes, the write-only password will be updated.
- `port` (Number) The port of the SMTP server. Defaults to `25`.
- `sender` (String) The desired sender email address.
- `test_email_address` (String) The email address to send a test message to. This value is not persisted and is only used during testing.
- `username` (String) The username used to authenticate to the SMTP server. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the SMTP settings. Always `smtp`.



## Import

Resource tfe_admin_smtp_settings can be imported in the following format: 

```shell
# via the fixed ID 'smtp'
terraform import tfe_admin_smtp_settings.this smtp
```
